clue.text: For brilliant rose exterior, large rear's whacked outside

indicators.note: the exterior of a word is its outside pair of letters, here the first and last of rose
the word for whacked is placed outside, so it wraps around the large-plus-rear pair

parts.note: whacked means exhausted, worn out, spent
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
the rear of something is its end

explanation.surface: Someone admires a dazzling rose garden while a large backside is being spanked out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' and the 's are link words; 'rose' looks like the flower but only its outside letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a resplendent sight is dazzling, shining and splendid.

clue.text: European fiction's about, say, serious poems

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the fiction word goes around the example abbreviation

parts.note: fictions are lies; the 's makes it plural
say signals an example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A European novel deals with, for instance, solemn verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegies are mournful, serious poems, typically laments for the dead.

clue.text: Head accepts old, big top chief

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the head word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
a big top is a circus tent

explanation.surface: The head of a circus takes on an ageing ringmaster in charge of the big top.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a potentate is a ruler or monarch, one in supreme command.

clue.text: Topless shock revealing boob

indicators.note: topless means the top letter is removed, which in a down clue is the first

parts.note: terror is a great fright or shock

explanation.surface: A tabloid shock as a topless picture reveals a breast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boob' looks like the tabloid sense of breast, but it is slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: a boob is a silly mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Arrested cheat, say, brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means the letters are written from bottom to top
say tells us to use a spelling that sounds the same as the word for cheat

parts.note: to cheat someone is to defraud them

explanation.surface: A cheat is arrested, for example, and brought up before the court.
explanation.walkthrough: DEFRAWD, which sounds the same as DEFRAUD ('say'), is written upwards ('brought up') to give DWARFED.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrested growth is stunted, as in a plant whose development has been checked.

clue.text: Figure, half naked, spread embracing Romeo

indicators.note: half tells us to keep only the first two of the four letters

parts.note: naked means nude

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the spread word goes around the Romeo letter

parts.note: a spread is a lavish meal
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A half-naked figure is spread out, clasping her lover Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like a verb but is the noun for a lavish feast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a numeral is a figure, a symbol standing for a number.

clue.text: Printer's perseverance uncovering dot

indicators.note: uncovering means revealing letters that sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A printer keeps going until a stray dot shows up on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: To dot something about is to scatter it here and there, which is to intersperse it.

clue.text: Relief for Tory restraining Labour

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the answer is held within the words around it

explanation.surface: A political sketch: relief for the Conservatives as they keep the Labour Party in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party, but it is the plain noun for hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: labour is hard work or exertion.

clue.text: Most vulgar gathering after supporter's return

indicators.note: after puts the gathering word behind the turned supporter
return means the supporter word is turned back to front

parts.note: a fan is a supporter, as of a football club
a fest is a festive gathering

explanation.surface: The rowdiest party is the one held after a fan comes home.
explanation.walkthrough: NAFF is British slang for tacky or uncool.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: naff means tasteless or tacky, so the superlative is the most vulgar.

clue.text: Queen comeback with poor money for arenas

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the queen letters are read backwards

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
alms are money given to the poor

explanation.surface: The Queen returns with charity cash for the stadiums.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative synonym: realms are spheres of activity, fields or domains.

clue.text: Show's over from nude tarts, no meddling!

indicators.note: over says the letters are turned around, read from the end back to the start
from says the letters are taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A notice says a show is finished, after its naked dancers object to interference.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link. The run ETARTSNOMED sits in 'nude tarts, no meddling' ('from') and is read backwards ('over').
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to show how something works is to demonstrate it.

clue.text: Feeling of degradation spending penny

indicators.note: spending means using up, so the penny letter goes out of the word

parts.note: a demotion is a degradation in rank
D is the abbreviation for an old British penny, from the Latin denarius

explanation.surface: Someone describes how it feels to be humiliated, after spending a penny in a public toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spending a penny' is a British euphemism for going to the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an emotion is a feeling such as joy, anger or fear.

clue.text: Release ends without charge involving English judge

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its first and last letters
involving means taking in, so the free word holds the English letter

parts.note: without charge means free

explanation.surface: An English judge sets the accused free with no charges.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to referee a match is to judge it, ruling on play.

clue.text: Express mentions plots

indicators.note: to express is to say out loud, so the word is chosen for how it sounds

parts.note: to cite something is to mention it as evidence

explanation.surface: The Express newspaper writes about schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plots' looks like schemes, but it means pieces of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: plots of land are sites, as for building.

clue.text: Creature's wing suffering in difficulty

parts.note: an arm is a wing or branch, as of an organisation

indicators.note: in means the suffering word goes inside the difficulty word

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble, as in without more ado
someone ill is suffering

explanation.surface: An animal's wing is injured and it is in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is an example: a burrowing mammal of the Americas with a bony shell.

clue.text: Ugly girl, female bird catching old man rising

parts.note: miss is a young girl, or her title

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the female bird word goes around the turned father word

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: old man is slang for father, pa

explanation.surface: An unattractive girl and a hen grab hold of an old fellow as he gets up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: misshapen means deformed or badly formed, so ugly.

clue.text: Ardour's small on grand bird in endless repose

indicators.note: in says the next pieces sit inside the trimmed repose word
endless removes the last letter

parts.note: repose means ease or rest

indicators.note: on places the small letter after the bird word

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds
the erne is the sea eagle, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: An eagle at rest is keen, with a small chick perched on a large one.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link. 'endless' turns EASE into EAS, and GERNES goes in between its A and its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ardour is enthusiasm or keenness, a passionate eagerness.

clue.text: Gargantuan butt wearing tasteless dress

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the tasteless word goes round the butt letter

parts.note: garish means gaudy or tasteless

indicators.note: a butt is the thick end of something, here the last letter

explanation.surface: An enormous bottom squeezed into a gaudy frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' looks like a noun, but it is the cookery verb, to decorate a dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Cookery verb: to garnish a dish is to dress it with decoration such as herbs.

clue.text: Material covering hat's alligator perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, covering puts the material word above the hat word

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A hat made from an alligator's skin, under a covering of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an alligator is a kind of scaly cold-blooded animal, so 'perhaps' marks it as one instance.

clue.text: Puzzle of unfinished Titian sculpture

indicators.note: unfinished applies to both words, so each loses its final letter

parts.note: titian is a reddish-brown colour, named after the painter
a bust is a sculpture of head and shoulders

explanation.surface: A mystery about an incomplete statue by Titian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Titian' looks like the painter, but it is the hair colour named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures or symbols stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: Chap holding puff first runs a fast time

indicators.note: first tells us the runs and a letters come before the chap word

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the chap word goes around the puff word

parts.note: a chap is a man
a puff is a promotional notice, an ad

explanation.surface: A man holds his breath before running a quick lap.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of daytime fasting, so it is a time of fast.

clue.text: Cross beam supporting back

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the beam word underneath the back word

parts.note: to back a horse is to bet on it
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A builder props up a cross-beam with a back support.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to double-cross someone is to betray them.

clue.text: Zebra crossing is empty with late or early parking unavailable

indicators.note: unavailable means one letter for parking is not there, so it comes out

parts.note: stripped means emptied, as of a room cleared of contents
P is the abbreviation for parking; there are two in the word, so either the later or earlier can go

explanation.surface: A pedestrian crossing is deserted, since parking is banned both late and early.
explanation.walkthrough: A zebra crossing is a British pedestrian crossing marked with black and white stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a zebra crossing is marked with broad bands painted across the road.

clue.text: Possibly poke with the thing?

parts.note: to dig someone is to poke or prod them
it is the pronoun for the thing

explanation.surface: A query about whether to jab with some object.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a finger is something you might poke with.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger is a digit, the very thing one pokes someone with.

clue.text: Bit of a pig, nearly cruel creature

parts.note: ham is meat from a pig's leg

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: stern means harsh or severe

explanation.surface: Part of a pig is almost a brutal animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hamster is a small rodent, an animal kept as a pet.

clue.text: Covering up physical abuse

definitions.meaning: a beating or thrashing, as in giving someone a good one

explanation.surface: Concealing a case of violence.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: concealment, and the informal noun for a thrashing.

clue.text: Put online digitally created articles some trolled initially

definitions.text: Put online digitally created articles some trolled initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the preceding words

parts.words: Put online digitally created articles some trolled

explanation.surface: Instructions for publishing internet pieces, some of which attracted abuse from trolls.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a show put online digitally.
explanation.definitionFit: A podcast is a digital audio show made available online for download.

clue.text: Ominous phobia about a number's admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so these pieces go inside the phobia word

parts.note: to have a thing about something is to have a phobia of it
re means about, concerning
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A person admits to an irrational fear of a certain figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an ominous sky is a menacing one, hinting at trouble to come.
